title: Temperature Converter (Celsius to Fahrenheit)
description: Write a function or program that accepts a temperature value in Celsius and converts it to Fahrenheit using the formula: F = (C * 9/5) + 32.
constraints: -100.0 <= Celsius <= 100.0. Input can be a float or integer.
hints: Remember the mathematical formula: F = (C * 9/5) + 32.
Ensure float division is used (9.0 / 5.0) to preserve decimal accuracy.
guided_steps: Step 1: Multiply the Celsius input by 9.0.
Step 3: Add 32.0 to obtain the final Fahrenheit temperature.
followup_question: What happens if you use integer division `9 / 5` instead of `9.0 / 5.0` in Python 2 vs Python 3 or Java?
followup_options: Integer division truncates 9/5 to 1, producing incorrect results

title: Leap Year Checker
description: Write a function that determines whether a given year is a leap year. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except for century years (divisible by 100), which must also be divisible by 400.
hints: Use the modulo operator `%` to check divisibility.
Check divisibility by 400 first, then 100, then 4.
guided_steps: Step 1: Check if `year % 400 == 0`. If true, return True.
Step 2: Else check if `year % 100 == 0`. If true, return False.
followup_question: Why is the year 1900 NOT a leap year while year 2000 IS a leap year?
followup_options: 1900 is divisible by 100 but not 400; 2000 is divisible by 400
2000 is a leap century rule exception

title: Sum of First N Natural Numbers
description: Write a program that takes an integer N and calculates the sum of all integers from 1 to N using an iterative loop.
hints: Initialize an accumulator variable `total = 0` before the loop.
Iterate from 1 up to N (inclusive) and add each number to `total`.
guided_steps: Step 2: Use a `for` loop `for i in range(1, n + 1)`.
Step 3: In each iteration, perform `total = total + i`.
followup_question: What is the closed-form mathematical formula (Gauss formula) to calculate this sum in O(1) time?

title: Prime Number Primality Test
description: Write a function that checks if a given integer n > 1 is a prime number (divisible only by 1 and itself). Optimize your loop up to sqrt(n).
hints: Numbers <= 1 are not prime.
You only need to check potential divisors up to the square root of n.
guided_steps: Step 3: Loop from i = 5 while i * i <= n, checking `n % i == 0` or `n % (i + 2) == 0`.
Step 4: Increment i by 6 each iteration.
followup_question: Why is it sufficient to check divisors only up to sqrt(n)?
followup_options: If n = a * b, one factor must be <= sqrt(n) and the other >= sqrt(n)
Because all numbers past sqrt(n) are prime
It is an empirical rule with exceptions

title: String Palindrome Verification
description: Write a function that checks if a string is a palindrome, ignoring non-alphanumeric characters and case sensitivity.
example_input: s = 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'
hints: Filter the string to keep only alphanumeric characters and convert to lowercase.
Compare the filtered string with its reverse, or use two pointers from start and end.
guided_steps: Step 1: Iterate over string characters and clean non-alphanumeric characters.
Step 2: Convert all characters to lower case.
Step 3: Compare character at index `left` and index `right` moving towards center.
Step 4: If all match, return True.
followup_question: How does the two-pointer technique achieve O(1) extra space compared to creating a reversed string copy?
followup_options: By checking characters in-place without allocating new string memory

title: Find Maximum Element in Array
description: Given an array of integers, write a function to find and return the maximum value in the array without using built-in max functions.
hints: Initialize a `max_val` variable with the first element `arr[0]`.
Loop through the remaining elements and update `max_val` whenever a larger element is found.
guided_steps: Step 1: Check if array is empty.
followup_question: What is the time complexity of finding the maximum element in an unsorted array of size N?

title: In-Place Array Reversal
description: Reverse an array of integers in-place without creating a secondary copy of the array.

reference_solution.Python:
def reverse_array(arr):
    left, right = 0, len(arr) - 1
    while left < right:
        arr[left], arr[right] = arr[right], arr[left]
        left += 1
        right -= 1
    return arr

hints: Use two pointers: `left` at index 0 and `right` at index `len(arr) - 1`.
Swap elements at `left` and `right` until pointers cross (`left >= right`).
followup_question: Why is in-place swap preferred over returning a new reversed array when memory budget is constrained?
followup_options: It operates in O(1) auxiliary space
It runs in O(log N) time

title: Vowel Counter in String
description: Write a function that counts the total number of vowels ('a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u', both lower and uppercase) in a given string.
hints: Define a set or string containing all vowel characters (both upper and lower case).
Iterate over each character in the string and increment a counter if it exists in your vowel set.
guided_steps: Step 3: For each character in input string, check if character is in set.
followup_question: Why is checking membership in a `set` faster than checking membership in a `list` in Python?
followup_options: Set lookups are O(1) average time complexity via hash table
Sets store elements in sorted order

title: Valid Anagram Detector
description: Given two strings s and t, return True if t is an anagram of s (contains same characters with exact same frequencies), and False otherwise.
hints: First compare string lengths. If lengths differ, return False.
Use a frequency map (dictionary or array of size 26) to count character occurrences.
guided_steps: Step 2: Build frequency dictionary for first string.
Step 3: Decrement frequencies using second string.
Step 4: Check if all frequencies equal 0.
followup_question: What is the advantage of character frequency hashing (O(N) time) over sorting both strings (O(N log N) time)?

title: Binary Search in Sorted Array
description: Implement binary search on a sorted array of integers. Return the index of target if found, or -1 if target is not present.
constraints: 1 <= arr.length <= 10^5, arr is sorted in ascending order.
hints: Maintain search interval bounds `left` and `right`.
Calculate `mid = left + (right - left) // 2` to prevent potential integer overflow.
guided_steps: Step 4: Adjust `left` or `right` depending on whether `arr[mid]` is less than or greater than `target`.
followup_question: Why is `mid = left + (right - left) // 2` safer than `mid = (left + right) // 2` in fixed-width integer languages like Java or C++?
followup_options: Prevents integer overflow when (left + right) exceeds maximum integer bound

title: Bubble Sort Algorithm
description: Implement the Bubble Sort algorithm to sort an array of integers in ascending order. Add an optimized boolean flag to terminate early if no swaps occur in a pass.
hints: Compare adjacent pairs `arr[j]` and `arr[j+1]` in an inner loop.
Use a `swapped` boolean variable to break early if the array is already sorted.
guided_steps: Step 1: Outer loop `for i from 0 to n-1`.
Step 2: Inner loop `for j from 0 to n-i-2`.
Step 4: If no swaps were performed in inner loop, break.
followup_question: What is the worst-case and best-case time complexity of optimized Bubble Sort?
followup_options: Worst-case O(N log N), Best-case O(1)

title: Factorial Calculation
description: Write a function `factorial(n)` that returns the factorial of a non-negative integer n (n! = n * (n-1) * ... * 1). Note that 0! = 1.
hints: Check base boundary: 0! = 1.
Multiply numbers from 1 to n iteratively.
guided_steps: Step 1: Handle base cases n == 0 or n == 1.
Step 3: Loop `for i in range(2, n + 1)` and multiply `result *= i`.
followup_question: Why can factorial values overflow standard 64-bit integer variables for n > 20 in languages like Java or C++?
followup_options: Because 20 is the maximum loop limit

title: Recursive Fibonacci Sequence
description: Write a recursive function `fibonacci(n)` that returns the n-th Fibonacci number, where fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1.
hints: Identify the base cases: n == 0 -> 0, n == 1 -> 1.
The recursive step is `fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)`.
followup_question: What is the time complexity of naive recursive Fibonacci without memoization, and why?
followup_options: O(2^N) due to redundant recalculation of subproblems in binary recursion tree

title: Recursive Sum of Digits
description: Write a recursive function `sum_of_digits(n)` that computes the sum of the digits of a non-negative integer n. For example, sum_of_digits(126) = 1 + 2 + 6 = 9.
hints: The last digit of n is obtained by `n % 10`.
The remaining digits are obtained by integer division `n // 10`.
guided_steps: Step 1: Base case: if n < 10, return n.
followup_question: How many recursive calls are made for an integer with d digits?
followup_options: d calls (equal to number of digits)

hints: Use three nested loops: loop i over rows of A, loop j over columns of B, and loop k for dot product calculation.

Step 3: Outer loop i from 0 to N-1, middle loop j from 0 to N-1, inner loop k from 0 to N-1.
